bullets.title: Fed holds at 3.5%-3.75% with hawkish 9-3 split; Warsh rejects 'pause' framing
bullets.body: FOMC voted 9-3 to hold benchmark rate, with Dallas Fed's Logan, Cleveland's Hammack, and Minneapolis's Kashkari dissenting for a 25bp hike—first triple dissent since 2016. Warsh explicitly rejected characterization as a 'pause,' said forward guidance belongs only in crises, noted real and nominal yields rose in a top-decile intermeeting move, and signaled the bond market is helping do the Fed's work. JPMorgan moved its first Fed hike forecast to December 2026. September hike odds fell below full pricing in swaps after Warsh's remarks.

bullets.title: 30Y yield hits 5.21%, highest since 2007; curve steepens as inflation fears dominate
bullets.body: The 30-year Treasury yield surged to 5.21% intraday—a 19-year high—and the curve steepened sharply after the hawkish-hold Fed decision and escalating U.S.-Iran military exchanges. S&P 500 closed down ~1.5%, Nasdaq-100 entered correction (-11% from June record), and the index is on pace for worst July since 2007. Retail investors sold a net $243M of single stocks, the largest one-day outflow since COVID.

bullets.title: MSFT surges ~10% AH on Azure +43% beat; FY27 guided to 45% with capacity demand exceeding supply
bullets.body: Microsoft F4Q26: revenue $90B (+18% YoY, +2.7% vs consensus), non-GAAP EPS $4.74 (+11% vs consensus). Azure grew 43% in constant currency, the fastest since early 2022 and 3.5pp above expectations; F1Q27 guided to 45% CC. Copilot paid seats reached 30M (up from 20M), net seat adds more than doubled QoQ, and GitHub Copilot revenue accelerated 60%+ QoQ. CY26 capex reaffirmed at ~$175B (ex-accounting reclassification of DC leases from 15 to 25-year useful life); FY27 FCF guided positive. Analysts raised PTs across the board—JPM to $550, Citi to $600, UBS to $525, Mizuho to $510, Wolfe to $550.

bullets.title: META down ~10% AH on EPS miss, FCF collapse 91%, and capex uncertainty overhang
bullets.body: Meta Q2: revenue $60.8B (+28% YoY, beat by ~1%) but GAAP EPS $6.18 missed $7.19 consensus by $1.01; GAAP operating margin 30.9% vs 35.6% consensus. Q3 guide of $61-64B was light of the $63.1B Street expectation. FY26 capex raised to $130-145B from $125-145B; FCF fell to $784M (-91% YoY), lowest since Q3 2022. Reality Labs lost $4.6B in Q2, cumulative since 2020 now $87B. No 2027 capex guidance provided; management said 'soon' 12x on product updates. Sell-side still 90% Buy but average PT cut ~3.5% to ~$794.

bullets.title: Semis -5.3% as SOX corrects; SOXX down ~30% MTD—worst month in recent history
bullets.body: The semiconductor index fell 5.3% on the day and is down nearly 30% month-to-date amid geopolitical risk, AI capex ROI uncertainty, and deleveraging in Korea (KOSPI -37% MTD, worst month ever). ARM and QCOM both missed on guidance; LRCX beat and raised materially (+43% YoY WFE guide to low-$150B). The Nasdaq-100 entered a -11% correction from June records. Citi's post-Fed semis survey: 30% of investors ready to buy now, 25% watching price action, 40% doing nothing.

bullets.title: LRCX beat-and-raise: WFE raised to low-$150B, Sep Q guided $8.1B—well above Street's $7.5B
bullets.body: Lam Research Q4 revenue $6.72B (beat), non-GAAP EPS $1.82; guided Sep Q to $8.10B ±$0.4B with $2.15 EPS ±$0.15, both well above Street. Record 52% gross margin; raised LT GM target to mid-50s% and OM to mid-40s%. Raised CY26 WFE to low-$150B from ~$140B. DRAM identified as fastest-growing segment for 2027; NAND WFE recovering to ~$20B annualized. Multiple analysts see CY27/28 EPS tracking toward $10-16. AMAT flagged as positive read-through.

bullets.title: Middle East escalation: U.S. strikes Iran; Brent crude surges 7-8% to ~$90, Hormuz stability at risk
bullets.body: CENTCOM completed large-scale strikes against IRGC targets; Iran launched missiles at U.S. forces in Jordan; Saudi Arabia joined U.S. in striking Iran-backed militias in Iraq. Brent crude settled up ~7.9% at $90.74/bbl and WTI up 6.6% to $84.46. Jefferies notes the conflict is shifting from military contest to maritime governance struggle, with Houthis exploring Red Sea toll systems and China securing selective Hormuz passage. Core inflation risk flagged through freight, insurance, and LNG—not just crude.

bullets.title: ARM beats Q1 but guides Q2 royalties to low-to-mid teens; smartphone weakness broadens
bullets.body: ARM Q1: revenue $1.29B (beat), EPS $0.45 (beat). Q2 guided to $1.33-1.43B revenue and $0.43-0.51 EPS, roughly in-line. Key negative: smartphone royalty growth guided to low-to-mid teens in Q2 (down from higher trajectory) as weakness broadens from low-end to mid and premium Android. Datacenter royalties doubled YoY; AGI CPU demand exceeds $2B but supply-constrained. FY27 royalty guidance cut to high-teens. ARM trades at ~76-83x FY27/28 EPS—UBS cut PT to $320, MS raised to $212.

bullets.title: QCOM misses on margin; Apple modem share loss accelerates faster than expected
bullets.body: QCOM Q3 revenue $9.95B beat but EPS $2.21 in-line; Q4 EPS guided $2.05-2.25 vs $2.35 consensus. Apple modem share now expected materially below prior 20% guide; iPhone revenue expected to decline every quarter and become insignificant by end of FY27. QCT gross margin compressed 72bp on higher input costs. Data center segment to generate ~$600M in Dec quarter (first contribution). Non-handset revenues targeted to exceed 50% of QCT in FY27. JPM cuts PT to $215 from $265; Citi cuts PT to $175; UBS cuts to $170.

bullets.title: S&P 500 tracking worst July since 2007; value trouncing growth by 23pp YTD
bullets.body: Russell 1000 Value up ~26% over one year vs Growth up ~4%; value up ~19% YTD vs Growth -3% YTD. S&P 500 Equalweight (RSP) near all-time highs while Nasdaq-100 is in -11% correction. Mega-cap tech stocks remain 18-41% below all-time highs (Oracle -66%, Palantir -41%, Tesla -40%, Meta -32%, Microsoft -23%). High Beta Momentum factor down -33% in the past month. Retail sold $243M in a single day—largest COVID-era outflow.

bullets.title: 2Q26 S&P 500 earnings tracking strong: 77% beating by 7.1% aggregate; Big 6 Tech EPS +48% YoY
bullets.body: With ~48% of S&P 500 market cap reported, 77% are beating estimates by 7.1% aggregate, above the 79% 1-year average. Big 6 Tech+ EPS growth at 48.4% YoY vs broader market 25.6%. Hedge funds averaged 7% H1 2026 returns (above 10-year avg of 4.1%); AI names drove ~85% of fundamental L/S alpha. Russell 2000 YTD +17.1%, outperforming S&P by 10.2%; small-cap aggregate earnings leading by 7.1%.

bullets.title: Korea KOSPI -37% MTD—worst month ever; margin call cascade unwinds leverage
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI declined over 33% in July, exceeding the October 1997 IMF crisis (-27%) and 2008 GFC (-23%). Over 360,000 margin accounts were forced into liquidation (62% under age 35); Korean retail investors lost an estimated $38.7B on leveraged products. JPM EM strategy estimates hedge fund deleveraging ~90% complete. Regulators reportedly considered a short-selling ban to stem losses.

bullets.title: FOMC's lack of forward guidance sends markets hunting for next hike; September odds repriced
bullets.body: Warsh declined to provide a reaction function, said forward guidance belongs only in crises, and explicitly avoided forecasting. Bond market interpreted the press conference as hawkish even though rates were held; 30Y hit 5.21%. Fed swaps initially priced out September hike fully but settled at ~72% probability. JPMorgan formally moved first-hike call to December. Warsh said the FOMC spent 'inordinate' time examining monetary policy and framed the decision as 'watchful thinking,' not inertia.

bullets.title: EQIX raises FY26/LT guidance on AI enterprise demand; capex upsized to $5-7B annually
bullets.body: Equinix Q2 revenue $2.63B (+16% YoY), adj EBITDA $1.40B (+24%), record bookings of $424M (+23% YoY), 9.7K net interconnections. Raised FY26 revenue growth guide to 10.7-11.6%; LT 2027-29 revenue growth raised to 10-13% (from 7-10%), EBITDA margins to 53%+, AFFO/share to 9-12%. Annual capex raised to $5-7B from $3-4B. 8 of top 10 AI model providers and 8 of top 10 neoclouds in EQIX facilities. MS, JPM, UBS, Citi all maintain Buy/OW with PTs raised to $1,250-1,300.

bullets.title: EU/China macro resilient; eurozone Q2 GDP +1.8% annualized, Spain +2.8%, France +0.7%
bullets.body: Eurozone Q2 GDP printed at 1.8% annualized (ex-Ireland 1.3%), well above ECB's 0.5% forecast and JPMorgan's estimate. Spain grew 2.8% annualized, France rebounded to 0.7%. Spain July CPI came in at 3.5% YoY (est 3.2%) and EU harmonized at 3.8%, above consensus. Germany Q2 GDP was +0.2% QoQ vs +0.3% prior. Swiss KOF leading indicator beat at 104.7 vs 100.9 estimate. China's Politburo reiterated moderately loose monetary policy and urged faster fiscal deployment; PBOC injected 600B yuan via overnight repos.

bullets.title: Situational Awareness AI fund (Leopold Aschenbrenner) seeks capital after AI stock rout
bullets.body: FT reports that Situational Awareness, the ~$20B AI-focused hedge fund co-founded by former OpenAI employee Leopold Aschenbrenner, is seeking fresh capital from existing investors and lenders after suffering heavy losses in the AI market rout. The fund was up 439% net YTD through June 30 but used leverage to amplify returns. Fund 13F showed large put positions on NVDA (9M shares), AVGO (3.3M shares), AMD (4.8M shares), and ORCL (7.3M shares).

bullets.title: MasterCard Q2 beats on 20th consecutive quarter; cross-border volume +12%, guides to low-teens rev growth
bullets.body: MA Q2 revenue $9.28B vs $9.08B consensus; EPS $5.04 ex-items vs $4.77 estimate; cross-border volume +12% local currency; gross dollar volume +8%; operating margin 61.1% vs consensus 60.3%. Raised full-year guidance to high end of low-double-digit to low-teens net revenue growth.

bullets.title: Samsung Q2 chip profit +1,814% YoY; warns supply shortage will worsen in 2027-2028
bullets.body: Samsung Q2 chip division operating profit was 89.2 trillion won, with HBM4 expected to exceed 60% of total HBM in H2. Samsung expects memory supply shortage to intensify in 2027 and persist into 2028 due to long fab construction lead times. Company plans to allocate 60-70% of capacity to long-term agreements and secured LTAs with five major global data center customers with minimum pricing. Apacer CEO separately warned commodity DRAM supply could fall 70% in 2027.

bullets.title: JPMorgan sees tech/semis momentum correction nearly exhausted; recommends buying dips via call spreads
bullets.body: JPM's international morning note: tech/semis momentum correction appears over based on leverage data, short interest, CTA positioning, and retail options data. Semis net exposures dropped sharply (Korea 1.7x from 5x, Japan 3.4x from 7.0x). Recommends scaling down factor hedges and buying short-dated upside via call spreads/ratios on AI/tech. EM MSCI sold off ~15% from June peak, with median 12-month post-correction return historically ~28%.

bullets.title: OpenAI July ARR exceeded all of Q2; GPT-5.6 and Codex adoption accelerating
bullets.body: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar disclosed internally that July annualized recurring revenue exceeded the entirety of Q2 revenue, driven by adoption of GPT-5.6, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. This was flagged across multiple sell-side notes as a positive read-through for hyperscaler AI capex justification.
